learn.hook: The ticket to the transport museum costs ₹75. Which notes and coins will you give?
points: ₹5.50 means 5 rupees and 50 paise. The dot separates rupees from paise.
We have notes like ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200 and ₹500, and coins like ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20.
To count money, start with the biggest notes, then add the smaller ones.
There are many ways to make the same amount. ₹75 = ₹50 + ₹20 + ₹5.

example.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?

learn.reallife: We count money when buying tickets, snacks at the station or souvenirs at a museum shop.

quiz.q: How many paise make ₹1?
quiz.explain: 1 rupee is the same as 100 paise.

quiz.q: Joseph has three ₹500 notes and two ₹100 notes. How much money does he have?
How many ₹10 coins make ₹100?
How do we write 5 rupees and 50 paise?
quiz.explain: Rupees go before the dot and paise after it: ₹5.50.

quiz.q: The museum ticket costs ₹75. Which set of money makes exactly ₹75?
quiz.mistake: Does not add up each set carefully

quiz.q: How many rupees is 250 paise?
Riya must pay ₹700 using only ₹500 and ₹100 notes. What is the smallest number of notes she can use?
quiz.explain: One ₹500 note and two ₹100 notes make ₹700. That is 1 + 2 = 3 notes.

quiz.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?

teach.ask: Gappu found 150 paise in the piggy bank. Gappu thinks it is ₹150. Is that right?
teach.praise: Oh! 100 paise make ₹1, so 150 paise is ₹1.50, not ₹150. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many paise make one rupee?

learn.hook: At the museum shop you buy toy trains and postcards. The shopkeeper gives you a bill. Can you check it?
points: A bill lists each item, how many (quantity), the price of one (rate) and the amount.
Amount = quantity × rate. 3 toy trains at ₹45 each = 3 × 45 = ₹135.
Add all the amounts to get the total.
Always check a bill. Shopkeepers can make mistakes too!

example.q: Bill: 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?

learn.reallife: Grocery shops, restaurants and railway ticket counters all give bills.

games.title: Is the bill right?
items: Multiply how many by the price of one.
Change from ₹500 for a ₹385 bill is ₹125

quiz.q: Meena buys 3 toy trains at ₹45 each. What is the amount?
A bill has 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?
On a bill, what does 'rate' mean?
quiz.explain: Rate is the price of one item. Amount = quantity × rate.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rate with amount or quantity

quiz.q: Apples cost ₹120 per kg. Aisha buys 2 kg. What is the amount?
A bill line says: Qty 4, Rate ₹25. What should the amount be?
A bill says 3 postcards × ₹40 = ₹130. What should the correct amount be?
quiz.explain: 3 × 40 = 120, so the bill should say ₹120. The shopkeeper made a mistake.

quiz.q: At the transport museum, adult tickets cost ₹50 and child tickets cost ₹20. What is the bill for 2 adults and 3 children?
quiz.mistake: Adds one adult and one child ticket only (₹70)

quiz.q: Harpreet's bill total is ₹385. She pays with a ₹500 note. How much change should she get?

teach.ask: Gappu bought 4 toy cars at ₹25 each. The bill says ₹125. How can Gappu check the bill?
teach.praise: Well done! 4 × 25 = 100, so the bill should be ₹100. Gappu saved ₹25!
teach.nudge: How do we find the amount from the number of cars and the price of one?

learn.hook: Saving for a model train? Sharing a taxi fare? Money maths helps every day!
points: Add to find a total cost. Subtract to find what is left or how much more is needed.
Multiply when the same price repeats. Divide to share money equally.
When adding rupees and paise, 100 paise make ₹1: ₹10.50 + ₹4.50 = ₹15.00.
To compare deals, find the price of one item in each.

example.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?

learn.reallife: Families share expenses for a trip, save money every week and compare prices before buying.

games.title: Which operation?
items: Savings of ₹25 a week for 8 weeks
How much more is needed to buy a bicycle
Cost of a samosa and a juice together

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?
₹360 is shared equally among 4 friends. How much does each get?
Which is cheaper per pen: a pack of 3 pens for ₹30 or 1 pen for ₹12?
options: Both cost the same per pen
quiz.explain: In the pack each pen costs 30 ÷ 3 = ₹10, which is less than ₹12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ₹12 is cheaper because it is a smaller number than ₹30

quiz.q: A toy train ride ticket costs ₹85. How much do 6 tickets cost?
Meena saves ₹25 every week. How much will she save in 8 weeks?
A bicycle costs ₹1250. Arjun has ₹875. How much more money does he need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Harpreet buys 2 samosas at ₹15 each and 1 juice for ₹25. She pays with ₹100. How much change does she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change, or counts only one samosa

teach.ask: Gappu wants to share ₹120 equally with 2 friends, so 3 in all. How much should each get?
teach.praise: Great! ₹120 ÷ 3 = ₹40 each. Fair sharing makes good friends!
teach.nudge: How many people share the money, counting Gappu? What operation shares equally?
